items.title: Lahore traffic police going beyond the road for recovery of e-challan dues
items.description: LAHORE: Chief Traffic Officer (CTO) Syed Abdul Raheem Shirazi has sent recommendations to the higher authorities to link the recovery of pending digital traffic challans to the core services of computerised national identity cards (CNICs), passports, sale/purchase of vehicles and police services, a move being considered ‘most controversial in the history of the traffic police’. The proposal is said to be a blatant violation of the constitutional rights of citizens and the judgments of the Supreme Court. Through an official letter, the CTO has suggested to the Punjab DIG traffic police to make a move to stop the issuance of duplicate CNICs, renewal of passports, vehicle transfer (sale/purchase transactions) and certain police services to the citizens/defaulters at the police Khidmat centres across the city, an uncalled for proposal that has raised eyebrows among the police circles and legal fraternity. Citing the CTO’s recommendations as an attempt to infringe upon the constitutional rights of citizens for generating revenue or recovery of pending payments, a law firm is all set to challenge the ‘executive order of an individual officer’ in the Lahore High Court (LHC). Propose making CNIC, passport issuance, vehicles sale/purchase conditional to clearance of e-challan dues; legal expert terms the move illegal A spokesperson for the City Traffic Police confirmed to Dawn that CTO Shirazi had proposed a comprehensive mechanism for the recovery of pending payments on e-challans. He said the decision was made to tighten the net around e-challan defaulters by making police, CNIC and passport services conditional to the digital challan clearance. “A formal communication in this regard has been sent to the DIG Traffic Punjab and the Punjab Information Technology Department (PITB),” said the spokesperson while quoting the CTO’s letter. The CTO has proposed that, as in the case of e-challan default, the provision of certain services at Police Khidmat Markaz should also be linked to the clearance of outstanding digital challan dues. The spokesperson added that timely recovery of outstanding digital challans would also help expedite the disposal of cases pending before courts. “It would increase government revenue while reducing the administrative efforts and expenditure involved in the recovery process,” he added. A senior lawyer, Omais Younis, declared the proposal of the CTO Lahore childish and funny, saying that the law does not allow such exercises/practices as the SC has protected the rights of the citizens in many reported judgements. “The Supreme Court has held that even a court executing a money decree cannot block a CNIC where the governing law does not authorise that mode of execution,” the lawyer said and added that an unadjudicated or disputed traffic challan provided an even weaker legal basis for such a deprivation. “Article 10-A guarantees fair trial and due process in the determination of civil rights and obligations and criminal accusations. A digital challan begins as an allegation; it is not necessarily a final adjudication merely because it appears in a government database,” said Mr Younis. “Withholding a CNIC for a traffic fine is not a traffic-specific inconvenience,” said the lawyer, adding that it might disable large areas of a person’s legal, economic and social life and might adversely affect family members. “The same is the case with the issuance of the passport which is a legal document that allows the citizen for free and safe travel,” the lawyer added. Referring to a judgement of the Supreme Court given on Feb 18, 2026, Omais said Supreme Court of Pakistan declared that even an executing court cannot block a judgment-debtor’s Computerised National Identity Card (CNIC) to enforce a money decree or demand security, ruling the practice illegal and beyond the jurisdiction of civil courts. “The court held that section 51 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides recognised modes of execution but does not authorise CNIC blockage”, he said, quoting the SC verdict. He added the SC had also stressed that a CNIC is not a luxury or a mere statutory formality. “We are moving the court of law against the unlawful and unconstitutional proposal of the CTO for the sake of protecting the rights vested under the laws to citizens,” said Omais. Published in Dawn, August 24th, 2026

items.title: You can’t talk integration and treat Africa like toilet roll – Dr Yamson blasts South African politicians
items.description: Economist and Board Chairman of MTN Ghana, Dr Ishmael Yamson, has condemned the xenophobic attacks on Ghanaians and other Africans in South Africa. The business magnate described the conduct as incompatible with the country’s push for African integration. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Thursday, Dr Yamson said South African politicians could not promote investment and continental integration while allowing Africans in the country to be subjected to hostility and violence. “I am particularly angry because the politicians in South Africa should have known that they cannot talk about integration, invest, encourage their country’s corporations to invest in Africa, and at the same time, treat the rest of Africa as if it’s their toilet roll they can walk on any time they like.” His comments come amid growing concerns over attacks on African migrants in South Africa, including Ghanaians, and the return of some affected Ghanaians to the country. Dr Yamson also rejected claims that corporate institutions in South Africa had remained silent over the attacks. He said the MTN Group chairman had condemned the violence, while the South Africa Ghana Business Chamber had also issued a statement. He, however, admitted that MTN Ghana should have issued its own statement earlier. “I apologise that we haven’t done that.” Dr Yamson stressed that MTN Ghana should not be associated with the actions of perpetrators in South Africa. “MTN Ghana is a corporate citizen of Ghana. It is not MTN South Africa.” He said the company has more than 120,000 Ghanaian shareholders and that the overwhelming majority of its employees and dealers are Ghanaian. Dr Yamson also condemned calls for Ghanaians to retaliate against South African-linked businesses operating in Ghana. He said such action would only hurt Ghanaian workers, shareholders and the wider economy. “But well, that will be a genuine feeling, but it will not help us, and it’s not going to help Ghana.” He argued that MTN Ghana had not done anything to warrant retaliation and continued to make significant contributions to Ghana’s economy. “If you target MTN Ghana, you can target it, but at the end of the day, you are destroying something that you should protect.” Dr Yamson said the company is also a major taxpayer and invests in social programmes across the country. “Every year, we put 1% of our profit after tax into a foundation that we invest in social investment.” He said MTN Ghana supports hospitals, schools, girls’ education and women’s empowerment. “So, yes, what is happening in South Africa is bad, but we need not equate that to MTN Ghana.” Dr Yamson further disclosed that MTN Ghana had committed GH¢10 million to support Ghanaians returning from South Africa. He said the company initially considered using the money as immediate support but later decided to establish a more sustainable intervention to help returnees rebuild their lives. He admitted that the company should have moved faster but said the support had not been abandoned. “We have not forgotten. We will do it. We’ll do it in a big way. We’ll do it in a way that will make more meaning.”

items.title: Presidency, Atiku bicker over subsidy removal
items.description: •100million Tinubus can’t stop me — Atiku •Ex-VP politicising economy with flip-flops on subsidy—Presidency By Johnbosco Agbakwuru & Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has declared that no amount of resistance from President Bola Tinubu or “millions of his gang of economic jesters” could stop him from restoring a targeted fuel subsidy to Nigerians, accusing the administration of dressing up subsidy removal as reform while quietly extending fiscal concessions to oil investors. But the Presidency in a swift reaction, accused the former vice president of politicising Nigeria’s economy after he renewed calls to restore the petrol subsidy, saying the stance sharply contradicted the economic position he took during the 2023 presidential campaign. However, Atiku in a statement issued by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Phrank Shaibu, in Abuja yesterday, said the President’s claim to have abolished subsidy could not be reconciled with tax credits and other incentives still available to petroleum operators. He anchored his case in the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited NNPCL’s own audited accounts, arguing that the figures contradicted the government’s insistence that subsidy had ended. “In 2023, NNPC’s accounts recorded approximately N4.84 trillion as energy-security expenses and related shortfalls, while its 2024 audited financial statements subsequently recorded about N7.13 trillion under energy-security expenses. ‘’NNPC itself explained that this expense arises partly from the difference between the exchange rate used to determine the regulated PMS ex-coastal price and the prevailing exchange rate when the import obligation is settled. ‘’In plain English, government was still absorbing a price differential after Tinubu had triumphantly announced that subsidy was gone,” the statement read. Atiku said the naming of the expense as a “shortfall” rather than subsidy did not change its substance, insisting that Nigerians were not interested in the terminology used to describe public money spent bridging the same price gap. “Nigerians do not eat semantics. Whether government calls it subsidy, under-recovery, shortfall or energy security, public resources were being used to bridge a gap between economic cost and the price at which petrol was sold. You cannot abolish subsidy at the podium and resurrect it in the accounts under an alias,” he said. He also cited the Deep Offshore Oil and Gas Projects Incentives framework, under which qualifying petroleum developments could access production tax credits beginning at $3 and $4.50 per barrel, as evidence that the government readily intervened in the market when investors stood to benefit. Contrasting that posture with the government’s stance on household relief, Atiku accused the administration of applying one economic standard to corporations and another to citizens. “The government can protect a multi-billion-dollar oil investment from risk, yet it says protecting the Nigerian worker from crushing hardship is bad economics. ‘’It can bend policy to make every barrel of crude more profitable, but tells a struggling mother that making the litre of petrol she needs to take her children to school more affordable is irresponsible,” he said. Atiku politicizing nation’s economy with his flip-flops on subsidy – Presidency Replying him last night, Sunday Dare, the President’s Special Adviser on Media and Public Communications, said in a statement that Atiku had earlier called for the removal of petrol subsidy, describing the regime as unsustainable, opaque and prone to corruption Titled “Atiku’s Subsidy U-Turn: The Bankruptcy of Desperate Ambition, “ Dare said: “In the architecture of modern political opportunism, few spectacles rival the breathtaking hypocrisy of Alhaji Atiku Abubakar’s recent policy pivot. “To watch a self-styled statesman, who less than four years ago cast himself as an uncompromising apostle of market-driven reform, scramble to promise the reintroduction of petrol subsidies is nothing short of political apostasy. “This isn’t merely a tactical policy disagreement; it is a sordid, stingy manipulation of the public psyche, designed to hoodwink unsuspecting citizens through an unpardonable exploitation of temporary economic pain. “Atiku’s vacillation stands as a monument to a fading presidential ambition gone completely awry, exposing a man willing to burn down national economic stability for a fleeting headline.” On what he described as a chronicle of political duplicity, he said: “Let us refresh the collective memory of the Nigerian electorate, which Atiku so cynically presumes to be short. During the intense build-up to the 2023 general election, Atiku made the total removal of the fuel subsidy the absolute cornerstone of his economic manifesto. “He argued with unyielding conviction, repeatedly echoed across national media platforms, including broad coverage by outlets like Premium Times and The Punch—that the opaque, corruption-ridden import subsidy regime was bleeding the nation dry, enriching a parasitic cabal, and mortgaging the future of generations unborn. “Yet, as the political calendar ticks toward the next electoral cycle and the reality of his diminished prospects sets in, Atiku has engineered a shameless volte-face. The architect of yesterday’s fiscal discipline has overnight transformed into the high priest of populist pandering. “This radical reversal is the ultimate hallmark of a desperate politician who cares less about long-term fiscal sustainability and more about capturing power by any means necessary. It is a cynical bet that Nigerians have forgotten his own economic doctrine—a scorched-earth strategy that weaponizes current hardships against the very structural reforms he once championed.” The post Presidency, Atiku bicker over subsidy removal appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 3 weeks on, nightly protests over Mir Raza’s murder continue in Karachi
items.description: • Family, friends and citizens gather on Sharea Faisal every night to demand justice • Vow to continue their demonstrations until those responsible for his death are arrested KARACHI: Family, friends, acquaintances and civil society members have been gathering on Sharea Faisal near Nursery every night for the past three weeks, blocking the key artery and vowing that they would not give up until justice is provided to slain Mir Raza Ali , whose body with a gunshot wound was found on July 29 at a desolate spot in Gulistan-i-Jauhar. More than 26 days after the murder, the identity of his killer(s) is yet to be known, compelling civil society to take to the streets on a daily basis. The Nursery bus stop has been turned into a focal point, where a large banner inscribed with ‘Justice for Mir Raza’ is displayed at the centre. The protesters include Raza’s family and friends, and dozens of men, women, their children and people of different age groups who have been demanding the arrest of Raza’s killers and exemplary punishment for them. On Saturday night, people turned out in large numbers and blocked both tracks of Sharea Faisal, staging a sit-in there until the wee hours of Sunday. During a visit to the protest site in the small hours of Sunday, protesters were seen using clapping as a collective expression of defiance and solidarity, blending it with their chants to create a wall of sound that carries far beyond the protest site. At times, the chanting, applause and calls for justice merge with the sound of drizzle and the movement of the night air, lending the gathering an atmosphere of persistence and resolve. A large number of participants raise their hands while chanting slogans and voicing their demands; some hold placards and banners bearing the words ‘Justice for Mir Raza’, making their presence felt, while others explain the protest’s background and history to those arriving for the first time. During the protest, one person can be seen addressing the gathering from the stage in memory of Raza, while another wipes away tears as emotions run high. Some protesters alternately climb onto water tankers placed by the police to block the roads and address the crowd from above, raising slogans against the police and the government. From time to time, slogans rise from the stage: ‘ Mir, hum sharminda hain, tere qatil zinda hain ’ (Mir, we are ashamed, your killers are still free) and ‘ Allah ka qanoon hai, khoon ka badla khoon hai’ (It is Allah’s law; blood must be avenged with blood). In other moments, speakers seek to keep Raza’s memory alive while impressing upon the crowd that his killing was not merely the loss of an individual but, in their view, an assault on the hopes and aspirations of Karachi’s young people. The stage reverberates with chants: ‘ Zinda hai Mir, zinda hai; bhaiyon ki shakal mein zinda hai, beton ki shakal mein zinda hai; zinda hai Mir, zinda hai ’ (Mir lives on, he lives on; he lives on in the face of brothers, he lives on in the face of sons; Mir lives on). At other times, the crowd raises the slogan: ‘Mir, tere khoon se inqilab aayega, raigan na jayega, inqilab aayega ’ (Mir, your blood will bring revolution; it will not go in vain; revolution will come). ‘We will not let Raza’s blood be in vain’ Dawn spoke to some of the participants who said that they would come daily to record their protest and would not give up hope until the killers were arrested. Alleging that the authorities were showing disregard for the grieving family, the protesters said, “The powerful think people would get tired of protesting in a few more days, but we [protesters] assure them that we will stand and protest for Raza, despite it taking months or even a year. We will not let his blood be in vain. We will bring his family justice.” On one side, dozens of men and women sit on rugs spread across the road, responding to slogans raised from the stage with enthusiasm and unwavering intensity. On the other, groups of youngsters spread across both tracks of Sharea Faisal, chanting at the top of their voices for the authorities’ resignation over what they describe as their failure to deliver justice. The presence of women, men and children gives the gathering the character of a broad-based public protest. Many had come with their families while others said they were taking time out of their daily routines to join the demonstration. Among the regular protesters is a woman known as “Apa”. She told Dawn that she did not know Raza or his family personally and had only met him once when she visited his eatery. “But when I came to know that he had been murdered in such a way, I could not tolerate it,” she said. She said she had children of her own and could understand what the family was going through. “This is not a jungle where we are living. It is a city. Even in a jungle there are laws,” she added. Apa said she would continue attending the protest and would be the last person to leave unless justice was provided. She said she remained hopeful that the truth would emerge and those responsible for Raza’s death would be arrested. For Raza’s friend Hassan Surya, the protest began before the family’s demonstration. When Raza went missing, he said, friends and family initially thought that he might have left home after becoming upset over “something personal”. They continued searching for him and when “we found out that he had been murdered in such a way, I started the protest”, he said. He said the family was busy with the investigation and other matters at the time. Hassan and some friends initially staged the protest at Charminar Chowrangi, Baha­durabad and later shifted it to Sharea Faisal, where it grew in size. Some of his close friends have since stopped coming regularly, he lamented, but he has continued to attend. Hassan said protesters had repeatedly become hopeful when the government appeared to take action, but their hopes were followed by frustration. “They keep creating diversions and excuses,” he said. “But we will not back down.” Two other protesters said that they had been attending the demonstration for around 15 days. They said they had joined because anyone murdered in such circumstances deserved justice. One of them said the protest had initially attracted fewer people but was gradually turning into a public movement as more citizens joined. He added that the government had yet to take any meaningful action on their demands. Published in Dawn, August 24th, 2026

items.title: L’ARTR appelle les transporteurs opérant à travers les applications numériques à se mettre en règle dans un délai de 15 jours
items.description: L'Autorité de régulation des transports routiers de Mauritanie a averti les entreprises de transport opérant via des applications numériques qu'elles devaient se conformer aux conditions et exigences légales et réglementaires en matière d'autorisation. Dans un communiqué publié vendredi, l’Autorité a invité les entreprises qui ne se sont pas encore conformées aux conditions d’autorisation à régulariser leur situation et à satisfaire aux exigences légales dans un délai maximum de 15 jours à compter de la date de publication du communiqué. Elle a averti que le non-régularisation de la situation dans le délai imparti entraînerait des poursuites judiciaires, y compris la suspension de l’activité, sans qu’un préavis ou un avertissement supplémentaire ne soit nécessaire.

items.title: La larga escalada de la vivienda: las casas duplican el precio tras 12 años de subidas ininterrumpidas
items.description: La curva que dibuja el encarecimiento de la vivienda en España durante la última década se parece más a una larga ascensión que a una montaña rusa. La estadística deja poco margen para la duda: según el Índice de Precios de Vivienda (IPV) del INE, desde comienzos de 2014 las casas se han revalorizado ininterrumpidamente durante 48 trimestres consecutivos, tomando como referencia la variación interanual. Desde entonces, el indicador ha permanecido siempre en terreno positivo, atravesando ciclos económicos, cambios en los tipos de interés y episodios de incertidumbre. El resultado es una racha de doce años de revalorizaciones ininterrumpidas que ha transformado el mercado residencial español. En ese periodo, el precio de la vivienda se ha disparado en buena parte del país, lo que ha provocado que el índice se haya multiplicado por más de dos. Dicho de otra forma: las casas ya valen más del doble que en el momento en que tocaron suelo durante la Gran Recesión. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La crisis sin resolver de Ceuta aterriza en un Congreso que calienta para elecciones
items.description: El Gobierno usará esta semana el Congreso para ofrecer, a través de la comparecencia de siete ministros, el primer relato ordenado, con todos los datos disponibles y contrastados, sobre el origen y la situación de la crisis sin resolver de Ceuta , y desmentir una buena ristra de bulos . Lo hará 26 días después de que se produjera la avalancha de unos 80.000 inmigrantes en la ciudad autónoma. El Ejecutivo no cuenta, por ahora, con una única versión de por qué se produjo esa entrada masiva, aunque se decanta por un efecto llamada generado por mafias, multiplicado en las redes sociales y promovido desde países que no tienen por qué ser solo Marruecos. El planteamiento teórico de que todos los inmigrantes que llegaron retornen al reino alauí choca con las trabas legales, las diferencias políticas y el reparo de ese país a acogerlos a todos. Pedro Sánchez descartó cualquier llamada a Alberto Núñez Feijóo, por su mala relación y por cómo reaccionó el líder de la oposición en las primeras horas tras la crisis para aprovecharla políticamente de cara a un largo año electoral. items.title: La frontera interior de Ceuta
items.description: Para una ciudad como Ceuta, rodeada de costa, la playa es un buen termómetro para un domingo de agosto. Y ese termómetro marcaba todavía una temperatura social muy caliente. Hay zonas con aire acondicionado y otras con abanico. En una parte se suceden las escenas de campo de refugiados y en otra los locales comienzan a sacar la nevera portátil, poner la música y abrir la sombrilla con la familia en la arena. La crisis que de un día para otro metió a 80.000 personas mantiene un buen tramo de costa inutilizada , pero la de Calamocarro este domingo lucía, por fin, relajada. “Es la única playa que nos han dejado. Ya está bien de quedarse en casa. Tenemos que recuperar el espacio porque nos han robado la ciudad de un día para otro. Aquí, al que llegue a esta playa, lo mandamos para allá”, dice un padre que pasa la tarde con otros dos matrimonios, señalando la alambrada de la frontera. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El Pequeño Nicolás quiere recuperar su nombre
items.description: Con 19 años, Francisco Nicolás Gómez Iglesias perdió su pasaporte y su nombre. Más de una década después, acaba de recuperar lo primero, el documento que le permite salir de Europa y ver el mundo que durante años sus amigos le han contado. Él, que en abril sopló 32 velas, aspira ahora a recuperar también lo segundo, el nombre que consta en ese pasaporte, y desprenderse para siempre del alias que lo catapultó a la fama y lo sepultó en ella: El Pequeño Nicolás . Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las siete crisis del verano europeo
items.description: Con sus inevitables castillos medievales y a medio camino entre Frankfurt y Luxemburgo, Kaub es una pequeña localidad alemana a orillas del Rin. Ese gran río convierte a Kaub en uno de los nodos del comercio fluvial en Europa. En esa zona el Rin se hace más estrecho, menos profundo, y eso lo convierte en uno de los puntos neurálgicos del transporte por esa vía en Centroeuropa: es allí donde se mide la capacidad de carga de los buques. Ese río, como todos los grandes ríos de Europa, se ha quedado prácticamente seco en agosto . El tráfico marítimo se ha visto muy afectado; la siderurgia, el sector químico y otras industrias alemanas se han visto gravemente perjudicadas. Las empresas han tenido que fletar camiones, más caros por el lío geopolítico en otro nodo logístico: el estrecho de Ormuz . Cambio climático, estancamiento económico y geopolítica, en fin, se interconectan en Kaub. Y lo mismo ocurre con los choques que está encajando Europa en este verano de pesadilla: hasta siete crisis que se entrelazan como las cerezas de un cesto. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El ‘lobby’ petrolero proTrump se hace de oro con la guerra contra Irán
items.description: A Donald Trump le cuesta asumir las responsabilidades cuando las cosas no salen bien. Acostumbra a señalar a otros cada vez que está bajo el foco. Los acusa y amenaza hasta que pasa la tormenta. Así lo ha hecho con la inflación o con el fracaso de la piscina reflectante de Washington . Hace un par de semanas también culpó a las grandes petroleras del alto precio de los carburantes, por encima de los cuatro dólares por galón. Las reprendió por estar “ganando demasiado dinero”, y exigió la devolución de parte de sus beneficios. “Cuando ves una empresa que ganó doce veces más que el año anterior, debería devolver parte de esas ganancias al público”, señaló desde la Casa Blanca ante la preocupación porque el precio de los carburantes está afectando al bolsillo de las familias. “Más les vale bajar el precio de venta al público, el precio para el consumidor”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La UCO y las fiscales del ‘caso Leire Díez’ siguen el rastro del dinero
items.description: La Unidad Central Operativa (UCO) de la Guardia Civil y las fiscales Elisa Lamelas y Mar Scharfhausen, de Anticorrupción, siguen la pista del dinero en el bautizado como caso Leire Díez . Con el respaldo de la Audiencia Nacional, los investigadores han impulsado el rastreo de decenas de cuentas bancarias para averiguar quién o quiénes son los “financiadores últimos” de la supuesta trama liderada por la exmilitante socialista Leire Díez y Santos Cerdán , ex secretario de Organización del PSOE, que buscaban presuntamente “desestabilizar” procesos judiciales que salpicasen al partido y al Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez. Los agentes y el ministerio público ya detectaron un flujo sospechoso de miles de euros entre varios implicados en el sumario —con abonos procedentes, incluso, de la formación—, pero creen que quedan “determinados pagos” por aclararse. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La Fiscalía redobla su ofensiva contra los narcos del mar para acusarlos también de piratería
items.description: La muerte del oficial del Servicio de Vigilancia Aduanera Carlos Esquembri durante el abordaje del velero Rothmans servirá como ejemplo para que los narcotraficantes que atenten contra la vida de los agentes de fuerzas y cuerpos de seguridad sumen un nuevo delito: el de piratería. Esquembri, melillense de 58 años, murió el 18 de marzo de 2023 durante un operativo en aguas internacionales. Estaba a más de mil kilómetros al oeste de las Islas Canarias cuando el narcovelero de 25 metros de eslora y bandera de Malta que los agentes querían abordar hizo algo inesperado. Dio un giro brusco y embistió la lancha policial, haciendo que volcara por completo. Los siete uniformados cayeron al mar y quedaron atrapados en el interior. Todos pudieron salir, excepto Esquembri. La condena por piratería al responsable de esa “maniobra peligrosa”, que el Tribunal Supremo avaló el pasado abril, ha supuesto un hito que la Fiscalía Antidroga no piensa desaprovechar. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Intervention de l’armée pour secourir des orpailleurs menacés par la soif au Tiris Zemour
items.description: Un groupe de chercheurs d'or de la région du « détroit d'Ormuz », située dans la région d'« Amirq Ayah » à l'extrême nord de la Mauritanie, a pu se procurer de l'eau, après avoir souffert pendant plusieurs jours d'une pénurie d'eau potable, grâce à l'intervention de l'armée nationale. Cette intervention fait suite à plusieurs tentatives menées par les orpailleurs pour se procurer une citerne d’eau provenant de la région d’« Gleib Ndour », mais les propriétaires des citernes ont refusé de répondre à leurs demandes en raison des prix élevés exigés pour le transport de l’eau vers la région. Le président de l’Union nationale des orpailleurs, Mohamed Ould Hamza, a déclaré à « Sahara Media » qu’il avait frappé à plusieurs portes ces derniers jours pour venir en aide au groupe, notamment auprès des syndicats, des autorités et de l’armée, précisant que le chef d’état-major des armées, le général Mohamed Val Ould Raïs, était intervenu personnellement, et donné ses instructions au commandant de la deuxième région militaire, le colonel Cheikh Ould Sid Bouya, qui a à son tour ordonné à la compagnie de l’armée d’« Gleib Ndour » d’approvisionner les chercheurs en or en eau. Ould Hamza a ajouté que l’opération s’était déroulée dans la nuit de jeudi à vendredi : un camion appartenant à un particulier, transportant 20 tonnes d’eau, a été mobilisé ; 12 tonnes ont été déchargées au campement des chercheurs d’or, tandis que le reste a été distribué aux abords du site. Le commandant adjoint de la deuxième région militaire, le colonel Ely Ould Sneïba, s’est également rendu sur le site des chercheurs d’or afin de constater sur le terrain leurs conditions de vie et de s’assurer que l’eau leur été bien parvenue. Le président de l’Union nationale des chercheurs d’or a salué cette intervention, adressant ses remerciements au chef d’état-major général des armées, au commandant de la deuxième région militaire, ainsi qu’au wali de Tiris Zemmour, soulignant que ce dernier était resté en contact permanent avec l’Union pour suivre l’affaire.

Preliminary investigations showed the couple, married for more than 40 years, had planned to divorce due to relationship problems, although authorities had not received any prior reports of conflict between them. items.title: ‘I apologise’ – Dr Yamson admits MTN Ghana was late to condemn xenophobic attacks
items.description: Economist and Board Chairman of MTN Ghana, Dr Ishmael Yamson, has admitted that the company was late in publicly condemning xenophobic attacks against Ghanaians and other Africans in South Africa. Dr Yamson said MTN Ghana should have issued its own statement earlier, despite a condemnation already issued by the South Africa Ghana Business Chamber. “I apologise that we haven’t done that.” He was responding to criticism that corporate institutions, including MTN, had remained silent while Ghanaians and other African nationals faced attacks in South Africa. Dr Yamson said the corporate sector in South Africa had spoken against the attacks. “The corporate sector in South Africa has been very outspoken against it. The MTN chairman spoke directly, and he condemned it in no uncertain terms.” He also said the South Africa Ghana Business Chamber had issued a statement condemning the attacks. But he acknowledged that MTN Ghana was expected to speak directly because of its size and influence in Ghana. “If you come to Ghana, MTN is big, and therefore, everybody would expect MTN to come out and issue a statement.” He stressed that MTN Ghana had no connection to the attacks. “Let me say now here that we condemn it unreservedly. We have nothing to do with it. We dissociate ourselves from it completely.” Dr Yamson said more than 120,000 Ghanaians are shareholders in MTN Ghana and stressed the company’s identity as a Ghanaian corporate entity. “MTN Ghana is a corporate citizen of Ghana. It is not MTN South Africa.” He also criticised South Africa’s handling of the attacks, saying the country could not promote African integration while treating African migrants with hostility. “What is happening in South Africa is bad. And I can tell you that we are angry.” He said he was particularly angry because of the contradiction between South Africa’s continental ambitions and the treatment of other Africans. He also condemned calls for retaliation against South African businesses operating in Ghana. Dr Yamson said such action would ultimately hurt Ghanaians. “If you target MTN Ghana, you can target it, but at the end of the day, you are destroying something that you should protect.” He said MTN Ghana has 120,000 Ghanaian shareholders and that about 98% of its employees are Ghanaian. He also pointed to the company’s contribution to Ghana’s economy. “MTN is the biggest taxpayer in this country.” He said MTN Ghana operates under Ghanaian law and has not wronged anyone in Ghana. “MTN Ghana has not done anything to anybody in Ghana, here in Ghana. Has not reneged on any of its commitments in this country.” Dr Yamson further revealed that MTN Ghana had planned to provide financial support to Ghanaians returning from South Africa. He said the board initially decided to set aside GH¢10 million as a welcome-back package. “When the issue broke, I can tell you, the board immediately decided that we will set aside ¢10 million to welcome for as a welcome back.” But the company later reconsidered the approach after realising that immediate assistance alone would not be enough. “What we then began to decide is that, and many of them, some I understand they were allowed only two suitcases when they are on their return. So how do we create a fund that we will use to help these people to start life all over again?” He said the company planned to add another GH¢10 million to create a fund to support the returnees in rebuilding their lives. “I think the mistake that we made was not to have engaged the Ministry of Foreign Affairs immediately about this.” “Sometimes when you are big, your internal bureaucracy can also delay a few things. But we have not forgotten. We will do it.” “We’ll do it in a big way. We’ll do it in a way that will make more meaning.” He also commended other organisations that had already supported the returnees. “For those who did it, Telecel and the others, I really congratulate them. Pentecost Church, I congratulate them.”

items.title: Des partis d’opposition réclament à ce que des comptes soient demandés aux responsables à l’origine des cycles répétitifs des coupures d’électricité
items.description: Les partis et forces d'opposition mauritaniens ont déclaré dimanche que le cycle répétitif des coupures d'électricité et d'eau ainsi que les perturbations des communications à Nouakchott révélaient, selon eux, un dysfonctionnement plus général dans la gestion des infrastructures et des services publics. Ils ont exigé du gouvernement qu'il ouvre des enquêtes indépendantes, identifie les responsables et fasse rendre des comptes à ce qui en sont responsables. Ces prises de position de l’opposition font suite à des coupures répétées d’électricité et d’eau dans la capitale, qui ont coïncidé avec des perturbations des services Internet et des télécommunications, tandis que les conséquences de l’incendie qui s’est déclaré dans les deux sous-stations électriques de l’Est et de l’Ouest continuent de peser sur l’approvisionnement en électricité. Le parti « Tahrir » (Renouveau du mouvement démocratique) a déclaré que la répétition et la durée des coupures ne pouvaient se résumer à des pannes techniques ou à des incidents imprévus, estimant que la crise reflétait, selon lui, la faiblesse de la planification, de la maintenance, du contrôle et de la gestion des infrastructures. Le parti a exhorté le gouvernement à prendre des mesures d’urgence pour rétablir le fonctionnement normal des services, à ouvrir une enquête indépendante et transparente sur les causes de l’incendie des deux postes de transformation électrique, à déterminer les responsabilités et à rendre publics les résultats de l’enquête. « Tahadi » a également appelé à la mise en place d’un mécanisme d’indemnisation des familles, des commerçants et des entreprises pour les pertes subies en raison de l’interruption des services, y compris la détérioration des denrées alimentaires, des médicaments et des biens, et a imputé au président Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani, à son gouvernement et aux responsables des secteurs concernés la responsabilité politique et administrative de la dégradation des services. Le parti a également demandé une révision de la mise en œuvre du « programme d’urgence pour la modernisation de Nouakchott », notamment en ce qui concerne les volets électricité et eau, ainsi que la divulgation des fonds et des financements alloués au projet, de leur utilisation et de son taux d’achèvement, estimant que la persistance des problèmes d’électricité et d’eau soulève des interrogations quant aux résultats des investissements et des projets annoncés. En matière de télécommunications, le parti a appelé les opérateurs et les autorités compétentes à expliquer les causes des perturbations sur Internet et dans les réseaux de télécommunications, et à s'efforcer de garantir la stabilité du service, soulignant que les citoyens, les institutions et les activités économiques dépendent de plus en plus de ces services. Dans un communiqué distinct, l’Union des forces du changement a déclaré que les habitants de Nouakchott subissaient des coupures répétées d’eau et d’électricité qui causaient un préjudice aux citoyens et aux activités économiques, et a accusé les autorités d’être incapables d’apporter des solutions durables malgré les ressources allouées au développement des infrastructures et des services. L’Union a demandé l’ouverture d’une enquête sur les causes des pannes, des incendies et des coupures répétées, ainsi que sur les marchés publics et les équipements utilisés, afin de déterminer les responsabilités et de traduire en justice les coupables. Elle a également appelé le président à assumer ses responsabilités, à révoquer les responsables de cette situation et à les remplacer par des personnes compétentes, selon le communiqué. L’Union a déclaré que la performance du gouvernement et les résultats de ce qu’elle a qualifié de politiques « d’urgence » exigent une mise en cause des responsabilités et des mesures correctives dans le cadre de la Constitution et de la loi. De leur côté, les Forces du salut ont déclaré que la crise de l’électricité n’était pas simplement le fruit de pannes techniques passagères, mais l’une des manifestations d’une crise plus large dans la gestion des services publics, accusant le gouvernement de faiblesses en matière de planification, de contrôle et de responsabilité. Les Forces du salut ont imputé à la gouvernement la responsabilité politique de la dégradation du service et lui ont demandé de révéler à l’opinion publique les causes des coupures répétées, l’état du secteur de l’électricité et les ressources qui y ont été consacrées, ainsi que de prendre des mesures urgentes pour garantir la stabilité du service, déterminer les responsabilités et demander des comptes aux responsables. Les habitants de Nouakchott sont confrontés à des perturbations dans un certain nombre de services essentiels, alors que les demandes se multiplient pour que les causes des coupures soient clarifiées et que les responsabilités soient établies, notamment après l’incendie qui a ravagé deux postes de transformation électrique dans la capitale.

items.title: Una redada, 46 historias truncadas: “Me falta la vida sin mi hija”
items.description: La segunda hija de María Eugenia García nació prematura. Killy Tatiana Yangquen García llegó a este mundo a los siete meses, pequeñita y frágil, dependiente de la protección total de su madre. Vivió sus primeros 20 años pegada a María Eugenia, nunca lejos la una de la otra. Hasta que a Killy Tatiana la apresaron en una redada en el almacén aduanero donde trabajaba sin papeles una mañana maldita de octubre. “¿Entiendes el cuidado que he tenido con ella y que me la arranquen así? ¿Y yo no poder protegerla? No la he vuelto a ver, solo por videollamada”, solloza la madre desde su hogar en Elizabeth, donde se mantiene escondida desde que a su hija la detuvieran y enviaran de vuelta a Colombia, el país del que emigraron hace más de una década. Seguir leyendo Texto: Paola Nagovitch Fotografía: Corrie Aune Edición visual: Gladys Serrano Video de redada: Cosecha Nueva Jersey Gráficos: Javier Figueroa

items.title: ¿Nos encaminamos a un Hiroshima de la IA?
items.description: Aquí, en Silicon Valley, los expertos creen que en los próximos dos años vamos a presenciar un extraordinario despegue de la inteligencia artificial. “Bienvenido a las estribaciones de la singularidad”, me dijo un amigo de la Universidad de Stanford a modo de saludo. En términos más sencillos, califican este avance inminente como una “automejora recurrente”: el momento en el que la propia IA entrena a cada modelo sucesivo de IA, lo que genera un desarrollo exponencial hacia algo que, en muchos aspectos importantes, es más inteligente que nosotros, los humanos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Macarena García: “Me he hablado muy mal, pero ahora me trato mejor”
items.description: Macarena García (Madrid, 38 años) empezó su carrera casi por el final, con premios y aplausos que suelen tardar años en llegar. Desde su debut con Blancanieves en 2012, con la que ganó un Goya y una Concha de Plata, no ha dejado de trabajar en cine, televisión y teatro, aunque aquel debut triunfal también acabó convirtiéndose, según confiesa, en una presión que le costó tiempo desmontar. Nos encontramos en Barcelona, donde rueda un proyecto del que no puede decir nada y a las puertas de uno de los escasos fines de semana libres que le ha dejado el verano. Este año ha estrenado dos proyectos: la película Un hijo y la serie Se tiene que morir mucha gente . En ellas exhibe sus dos caras: una melancolía innata, de la que da cuenta una mirada que siempre parece al borde de la emoción, y una insospechada vis cómica. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La casa del dragón y un palacio de cuento: León también celebra el Año Gaudí
items.description: Muchos peregrinos y turistas se quedan con la boca abierta cuando llegan a Astorga. “Pero esto, ¿qué hace aquí?”, exclaman algunos alzando la mirada hacia un monumento inesperado. La localidad leonesa conserva un rico patrimonio arqueológico romano y es parada emblemática del Camino de Santiago, pero reserva una sorpresa para los viajeros menos documentados: un palacio de cuento que convive con la vieja catedral gótica como una fantasía. Es uno de los dos edificios que el arquitecto catalán Antoni Gaudí (1852-1926) proyectó en la provincia de León, junto a la Casa Botines de la capital, también conocida como la Casa del Dragón por sus referencias al animal mitológico. Se trata de una concentración excepcional, pues el creador de la Sagrada Familia de Barcelona y genio del modernismo solo dejó tres obras principales fuera de Cataluña: las dos de León y la villa El Capricho en Comillas (Cantabria). Seguir leyendo

items.title: Todo empezó en un concierto de Björk: el triunfo de la horchata artesanal
items.description: Sus amigos les dijeron que no iba a funcionar. Que de noche, cubata y cervezas, pero ese 30 de mayo de 2003, Andoni, Yolanda, Nerea y Antón se empeñaron en plantar un carrito de horchata en la Ciudad de las Artes y las Ciencias de Valencia, a las puertas del concierto de Björk . Fue un éxito contra todo pronóstico, y constataron que la horchata apetece en cualquier momento. La gran revelación llegaría, sin embargo, en los meses siguientes, cuando uno de cada dos ancianos que se acercaban a aquel carrito exclamaba: “¡Si esto es como se ha vendido horchata toda la vida, homme! ¡Felicitats !”. A la enésima vez, el grupo de noveles horchateros acudió a la hemeroteca de la Universidad de Valencia. “Nos dimos cuenta de que estábamos recuperando la forma más antigua de vender horchata”, recuerdan hoy, en la sede de Món Orxata, Andoni Monforte y Yolanda Morán (ambos de 53 años y de Valencia), para quienes la chufa y su bebida se han convertido en una obsesión. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El Govern abre el curso con Educación y Rodalies como asignaturas pendientes
items.description: El Govern de Salvador Illa reanuda este lunes su actividad tras las vacaciones con el reto mayúsculo de encauzar la crisis en educación, que se ha convertido en su principal problema. La comunidad educativa ha convocado una nueva jornada de huelga para el día 8, el día del inicio escolar, en un mensaje elocuente de que la movilización continuará si no se atienden sus reivindicaciones de más personal y más medios. A ese reto, se le suman los problemas de gestión por el fiasco del Informe Pisa y las averías diarias de Rodalies en el corredor sur que explotaron el día del eclipse por falta de previsión y de trenes. El Ejecutivo confía en poder solucionar los dos focos y pone el acento en que ya podrá impulsar las inversiones tras la aprobación de los presupuestos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Shayan Oveis Gharan, matemático iraní en EE UU: “A veces hago el cálculo de cuánto de mis impuestos ha ido a los bombardeos en Irán”
items.description: Nacido en Isfahán (Irán) hace 34 años, Shayan Oveis Gharan se ha convertido este verano “por sus contribuciones fundamentales a la teoría de algoritmos” en ganador de la Medalla Abacus 2026 , el mayor reconocimiento mundial a un científico de la computación menor de 40 años. Entre sus grandes hitos está mejorar, junto con su antiguo estudiante Nathan Klein, la mejor aproximación conocida al problema del viajante, con aplicaciones que van del reparto de paquetes al diseño de circuitos electrónicos o la secuenciación de ADN, cuyo límite llevaba sin mejorarse desde 1976; o resolver con su colaboradora Nima Anari varias conjeturas abiertas sobre las llamadas cadenas de Markov, una herramienta clave para simular sistemas complejos, con aplicaciones que van de la física estadística al aprendizaje automático. Seguir leyendo

items.title: España se queda sin geólogos: “Sin ellos no podemos salvar vidas ni ahorrar dinero público”
items.description: España se queda sin geólogos. En nueve años —entre el curso 2015-2016 y el 2023-2024—, la carrera ha perdido el 26,7% de los alumnos de primero, que han pasado de ser 613 a 449, y el 37% de los graduados (de 302 a 190). No hay duda de que se vive una auténtica pérdida de vocaciones que pasa factura al mercado laboral y supone un peligro para la sociedad. Si se escuchase a estos profesionales, los costes humanos en la dana de Valencia o los materiales de los terremotos en Granada y en el volcán de La Palma hubiesen sido menores. “El problema está en secundaria. La geología apenas se estudia y nadie escoge en la carrera lo que no conoce”, resume Albert Soler, decano de Ciencias de la Tierra de la Universidad de Barcelona. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El quiero y no puedo de los refugios climáticos en Madrid
items.description: Todos ellos huyen del calor , defienden que estos espacios, en el Círculo de Bellas Artes, en el Centro Cultura Matadero, en la sede del Ayuntamiento CentroCentro, deberían superar la almendra central de Madrid y apuestan por mejorar la oferta por encima de una foto bonita como resultado. Todos ellos hablan desde alguno de los tres refugios climáticos abiertos en la capital, desde esos lugares en teoría pensados para guarecerse de las altas temperaturas , pero totalmente insuficientes para la población que de ellos haría uso si la oferta estuviera más extendida por la ciudad. Mientras los usuarios reclaman más iniciativas públicas de este tipo, los expertos consideran que deberían abrir más tiempo, expandirse más allá del centro y priorizar el confort a las opciones culturales. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ‘Patoman’, el joven malagueño que persigue el oro en el Mundial de Pokémon
items.description: Leo Marín, más conocido como P4t0m4n (Patoman), aparece en la videollamada con una tranquilidad que parece adquirida en mucho más tiempo que los 18 años que lleva en esta tierra. Especialmente cuando se considera a lo que se enfrentará a finales de agosto: una final de mundo de Pokémon GO . Es apenas el tercer español en los 30 años de historia de este juego en alcanzar este punto, y el primero en hacerlo en la categoría del videojuego para móviles que hace 10 años tomó al mundo por sorpresa y que a día de hoy acumula más de 650 millones de descargas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Desvío de impuestos en el Gobierno de Milei
items.description: El Gobierno de Javier Milei celebra el superávit fiscal como una de las pruebas decisivas de su éxito económico . Pero para lograr que le cuadren los números mantiene inmovilizados recursos que el Estado ha recaudado con fines específicos, como el dinero para el mantenimiento de la red de carreteras de Argentina o el destinado a obras hídricas. Una denuncia presentada ante la Justicia por la falta de ejecución de fondos fiduciarios acusa al Gobierno de haber acumulado un superávit cercano a los 3.000 millones de dólares por esta vía y de haber invertido gran parte de ese dinero en letras y títulos públicos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ceuta: esta vez tiene que ser la última
items.description: Cuando uno pasea por Ceuta estos días y se cruza con amigos y conocidos, la conversación deriva con frecuencia en una improvisada terapia emocional de supervivencia de la que todos estamos necesitados. Flota una reflexión que muchos caballas comparten: evocan a seres queridos ya fallecidos y se muestran aliviados de que el destino les haya ahorrado el trago de presenciar el zarpazo que Ceuta sufrió el pasado 30 de julio. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El fenómeno Inde Navarrette, la actriz que dando miedo ha conquistado a público, crítica y a los directivos de Marvel Studios
items.description: “La fase 1 de mi plan maestro está completa”, bromeó Inde Navarrette (Tucson, Arizona, 25 años) el 10 de agosto en una entrevista con la revista independiente Schön! La actriz se refería a su meteórico ascenso gracias a su papel protagonista en la exitosísima Obsession , su debut cinematográfico en la película de terror que ha recaudado más de 426 millones de dólares partiendo de un presupuesto de menos de uno. Su inquietante interpretación tanto física como psicológica en la piel de Nikki ha conquistado a público y a crítica por igual, y le ha valido premios a mejor actriz en el Festival Internacional de Cine de Seattle o en los Astra Midseason Movie Awards. “He tenido muchas reuniones desde que salió Obsession ”, aseguraba la actriz a Variety a finales de julio. Una sola película y escasos meses de fama han bastado para que todos quieran a Inde Navarrette en sus proyectos, hasta confirmar su gran salto del cine independiente a la franquicia más mainstream del momento: “Como Pícara... Inde Navarrete”, anunció Kevin Feige, presidente de Marvel Studios , durante la presentación el pasado 14 de agosto del nuevo elenco del reboot de X-Men en el multitudinario D23 2026 . Seguir leyendo

items.title: Sarina Castagnoli, pastelera: “Me gusta traer de vuelta esas tartas que ya no se ven, las que comía cuando era niña en los noventa”
items.description: Hace tartas para las actrices, cantantes y marcas del momento, pero si su vecina de 85 años le pide un pastel de cumpleaños, se lo prepara con todo el amor del mundo. “También se las hago a mis amigas. Me encanta jugar con la personalidad de la gente que conozco para crear cada tarta”. Seguir leyendo

items.description: Se conoce que la cocina de casa es un espacio cuya propiedad ostenta, oficiosamente, la persona que maneja los fogones y alimenta a su tribu . Dada la monumentalidad de la misión, el cocinero o cocinera de la familia debería gozar de una autoridad dictatorial en su territorio, sobre todo cuando está con las manos en la masa . items.title: El Pesero: el primer chiringuito playero de la historia emergió de un naufragio en Cádiz en 1752
items.description: Bautista Pesero era un tipo bien listo y un buen cocinero, es lo poco que se puede leer entre líneas del escaso rastro de migas de pan que la historia ha legado sobre él. Allá por febrero de 1752, le ficharon para cocinar en el campamento creado en la playa de Chiclana de la Frontera para rescatar los restos del trágico naufragio del Soberbio , un navío mercante. A Pesero le impusieron el precio máximo del menú que debía cobrar por alimentar a los 200 hombres desplegados para recuperar el oro, la plata y las monedas hundidas bajo el mar. Pero nada le dijeron de que, junto a esa barraca de madera construida con los restos del mismo hundimiento, crease otra, sin topes de precios, para alimentar a la multitud de curiosos que se asomaban por la actual playa de La Barrosa. Y así fue como este vecino gaditano del siglo XVIII se convirtió —por ahora— en el primer dueño documentado de un chiringuito en la costa española . Seguir leyendo

items.title: La RS Berkane recrute l’international cap-verdien Ryan Mendes
items.description: La Renaissance sportive de Berkane (RSB) tient une nouvelle recrue d’expérience. Le club marocain a officiellement annoncé ce dimanche la signature de l’international cap-verdien Ryan Mendes, qui s’est engagé pour une saison avec une option de prolongation. Le contrat prévoit en effet une prolongation automatique d’une année supplémentaire si le joueur et le club atteignent les objectifs fixés en championnat national et en Ligue des champions de la CAF. À 36 ans, Ryan Mendes apporte toute son expérience à la formation berkanaise. L’attaquant cap-verdien s’est notamment illustré avec les Requins Bleus lors de la Coupe du monde 2026, avant de rejoindre le championnat marocain. Fort d’une longue carrière professionnelle, Mendes possède une expérience importante acquise aussi bien en Europe que dans les pays du Golfe. Son arrivée devrait permettre à la RSB de renforcer son secteur offensif avec un joueur habitué aux rendez-vous de haut niveau. Cette signature revêt également une dimension particulière pour Ryan Mendes puisqu’il va retrouver à Berkane son ancien sélectionneur avec le Cap-Vert, Pedro Leitão Brito, dit « Bubista ». Le technicien cap-verdien a récemment été nommé entraîneur principal de la Renaissance sportive de Berkane, en remplacement de Mouine Chaabani. La présence de Bubista pourrait ainsi faciliter l’intégration de Mendes dans son nouvel environnement et permettre au technicien de s’appuyer sur un joueur qu’il connaît parfaitement. La RSB se prépare à une saison ambitieuse, avec notamment la Ligue des champions de la CAF au programme. Le club berkani souhaite poursuivre sa dynamique et continuer à jouer les premiers rôles sur les scènes nationale et continentale. Avec l’arrivée de Ryan Mendes, Berkane mise donc sur l’expérience et la connaissance du haut niveau pour renforcer son effectif et atteindre ses objectifs cette saison. The post La RS Berkane recrute l’international cap-verdien Ryan Mendes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Enseignement supéreur: 1 800 diplômés orientés vers des études de master sur un total de 4 677 demandes
items.description: Le ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique a annoncé l'orientation de 1 800 diplômés de licence ayant obtenu d'excellents résultats vers des programmes de master en Mauritanie et à l'étranger, sur les 4 677 étudiants ayant déposé une demande pour poursuivre leurs études. Par ailleurs, chaque médecin généraliste dont le dossier était complet s'est vu attribuer une place pour suivre une spécialisation médicale en Algérie ou au Maroc, selon le communiqué du ministère. Le ministère a précisé que le nombre de diplômés de licence cette année s’élevait à 5 871 étudiants répartis dans 108 formations nationales, et que 4 677 étudiants avaient demandé à poursuivre leurs études en master. Le processus d’orientation a concerné 1 237 étudiants vers 62 programmes de master en Mauritanie, contre 563 étudiants vers des programmes à l’étranger, ce qui représente environ 31 % du nombre total de diplômés de licence et 38 % du nombre total de demandes d’admission en master. Le ministère a ajouté avoir réservé 20 places à la mobilité internationale, notamment dans les domaines de la physique et de l’ingénierie. Dans le domaine de la médecine, le ministère a indiqué avoir orienté 194 médecins généralistes vers des programmes de résidence médicale en Algérie et au Maroc, répartis sur 45 spécialités, soit 144 places en Algérie et 50 au Maroc. Il a précisé que chaque médecin généraliste dont le dossier était complet avait eu la possibilité d’intégrer un internat, à condition que cela n’entre pas en conflit avec ses obligations nationales liées au travail ou à l’internat. Le ministère prévoit de rouvrir la plateforme d’orientation le mercredi 26 août pour les lauréats de la deuxième session, ainsi que pour les lauréats de l’année dernière souhaitant changer d’orientation. Le ministère a précisé que cette même période offrira une seconde chance aux lauréats de la première session qui n’ont pas participé à la première phase d’orientation, afin qu’ils puissent rattraper leur retard.

items.title: Ishmael Yamson warns Ghanaians against targeting MTN Ghana over South African xenophobia
items.description: Economist and Board Chairman of MTN Ghana, Dr Ishmael Yamson, has warned Ghanaians against targeting MTN Ghana and other South African-linked businesses in retaliation for xenophobic attacks on Ghanaians in South Africa. He said such retaliation would hurt Ghanaian interests and could amount to destroying businesses that contribute significantly to the local economy. His comments come amid anger over attacks on African migrants in South Africa, including Ghanaians, with calls for retaliatory action against South African businesses operating in Ghana. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Thursday, Dr Yamson said MTN Ghana should not be held responsible for the actions of South Africans involved in the attacks. “If you target MTN Ghana, you can target it, but at the end of the day, you are destroying something that you should protect.” He said MTN Ghana has significant Ghanaian ownership and employs thousands of Ghanaians. “We have over 120,000 Ghanaians as shareholders in MTN Ghana. MTN Ghana is a corporate citizen of Ghana. It is not MTN South Africa.” He added that the majority of MTN Ghana’s employees are Ghanaian. “Every employee in MTN, maybe 98% of employees in MTN, is Ghanaian. All our other dealers are Ghanaians.” Dr Yamson said MTN Ghana also makes a major contribution to the Ghanaian economy through taxes. “If you talk about our contribution in terms of taxes, MTN is the biggest taxpayer in this country.” He acknowledged criticism that MTN Ghana had not publicly condemned the xenophobic attacks earlier. “I apologise that we haven’t done that.” “We haven’t made a statement as MTN Ghana. That is correct. And we should have, and I admit.” But he said the wider corporate sector in South Africa had spoken against the attacks. “The corporate sector in South Africa has been very outspoken against it. The MTN chairman spoke directly, and he condemned it in no uncertain terms.” Dr Yamson himself also condemned the attacks and dissociated MTN Ghana from them. “We condemn it unreservedly. We have nothing to do with it. We dissociate ourselves from it completely.” Speaking specifically as chairman of MTN Ghana, he repeated his condemnation. “I condemn it. I completely dissociate MTN Ghana from it. We have nothing to do with it.” He described the attacks as unacceptable and said two Ghanaians had lost their lives. “We just think that it belongs to the Stone Age. It’s not something that anybody should have been contemplating doing it, because the Ghanaians who are there, Ghanaians are very law-abiding. Now, two Ghanaians have lost their lives.” Dr Yamson said retaliating against Ghanaian businesses would not resolve the problem. “But well, that will be a genuine feeling, but it will not help us, and it’s not going to help Ghana.” He argued that Ghana must separate the actions of South Africans involved in the attacks from the operations of businesses such as MTN Ghana. “We have to be able to separate what is happening in South Africa by South Africans to Ghanaians, because MTN Ghana has not done anything to anybody in Ghana, here in Ghana.” He also pointed to MTN Ghana’s social investments as part of its contribution to the country. “Every year, we put 1% of our profit after tax into a foundation that we invest in social investment. We invest in hospitals, we invest in schools, we invest in girls’ education, we invest in women’s empowerment.” “So, yes, what is happening in South Africa is bad, but we need not equate that to MTN Ghana.” “No, that will be for me, rather killing the very goose that lays the golden eggs.” Dr Yamson also disclosed that MTN Ghana had begun work on a support package for Ghanaians returning from South Africa following the attacks. He said the board initially decided to set aside GH¢10 million as a welcome-back package. “When the issue broke, I can tell you, the board immediately decided that we would set aside ¢10 million as a welcome back.” But the company later reconsidered how the money should be used. “So maybe we should change the framework a bit.” He said MTN Ghana was considering a fund that would help returnees rebuild their lives. “So how do we create a fund that we will use to help these people to start life all over again?” Dr Yamson admitted that the company should have engaged the Ministry of Foreign Affairs earlier. “I think the mistake that we made was not to have engaged the Ministry of Foreign Affairs immediately about this.” He assured that the support had not been abandoned. “We have not forgotten. We will do it. We’ll do it in a big way. We’ll do it in a way that will make more meaning.”

items.title: Unlearnt lessons of history
items.description: TODAY, the country’s hybrid government is fixated on altering Pakistan’s constitutionally mandated provincial structure and multiplying administrative units. To sell the idea, establishment apologists have rolled out some disingenuous arguments. They claim this will improve governance and miraculously solve the country’s problems overnight. A debate has been generated in the media about the pros and cons of administrative changes and breaking provinces into more units. Parliament has yet to discuss this. That is unsurprising. Deliberation is not this legislature’s strong suit. It has rushed through constitutional amendments in record time, once in the dead of night and without meaningful debate. Meanwhile, speculation is mounting that another constitutional amendment is being prepared to push through ‘administrative changes’. Absent from the establishment’s consideration of these sweeping changes are lessons from Pakistan’s history. Over the decades, the country’s rulers have experimented with parliamentary, presidential, semi-presidential, quasi-parliamentary systems, direct military rule, and more recently a hybrid model, which involves informal power-sharing between the military and civilians, with the former as dominant partner. Pakistan has tried them all. Yet each switch only contributed to political instability. The only system to command legitimacy and broad support is parliamentary democracy, despite the fact that parliamentary supremacy over the executive has never been realised. Linked to these experiments has been the status and rights of provinces in a federal system. As the provincial configuration and federating units largely coincided with the ethnic composition of people of each province, the need was always felt to make federalism a reality, not just a constitutional precept to ensure the people of all four provinces felt they were part of an inclusive and fair system. Pakistan’s troubled history offers a cautionary lesson against altering the provincial structure. But the federal structure and provincial rights have always been contested issues in Pakistan’s history. Contested on many counts. Smaller provinces have long resented Punjab’s political hegemony, sought greater powers and autonomy and felt the distribution of resources has been unfair. Unelected institutions have always preferred a centralised polity while military rule meant the country functioned as a virtual unitary state. Long periods of unrepresentative rule fuelled alienation among the smaller provinces by marginalising them, suppressing regional identities, concentrating power at the centre and weakening federalism. The creation of One Unit in the 1950s, which merged all the provinces of what was then West Pakistan into a single unit, was aimed at creating ‘parity’ with the more populous eastern wing of the country to undercut its numerical majority. This politically motivated project imposed a unitary system and all but destroyed the country’s federal character. It was justified by totally false and frivolous arguments. They included claims it would end “provincial prejudices”, reduce adm­i­nistrative expenses and help develop backward areas. The move had disastrous consequences. It fanned the flames of nationalist and regionalist sentiment in the smaller provinces of West Pak­istan and strengthened centrifugal forces across the country. It contributed to the sense of discrimination among the people of East Pakistan that, along with other factors, found expression in the Bengali nationalist movement and ultimately led to the break-up of Pakistan in 1971. The issue of provincial rights continued to be a source of tensions and contestation. The 1973 Constitution struck a delicate balance between the centre and provinces in a multiethnic state, assured provincial autonomy and enjoined reciprocal obligations between the federating units. Unfortunately, this was observed more in its breach than in its adherence. Opposition-run provincial governments were ousted in the 1970s by prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. This reinforced a political tradition that began in the early years after independence when provincial governments were summarily dismissed by the central government. This seriously undermined national unity. These and other actions widened interprovincial disparities, deepened alienation among smaller provinces and led to the insurgency in Balochistan in the 1970s. This intensified during the 2000s but their antecedents reached back to the 1950s. The insurgency continues today as a result of monumental mishandling of the province and Baloch sentiment by successive governments. Authoritarian measures also gave a fillip to Pakhtun nationalism, even though over time this waned with the increasing representation of KP in the country’s power elite and bure­aucracy. The troubled history of federalism and provincial tensions in Pakistan offers a cautionary lesson against altering the country’s four ethnically distinct provinces. Past attempts to do that or erode constitutionally guaranteed provincial rights only widened fault lines and created new ones. These efforts were never about better governance or a stronger administrative system. They were about control. They reflected the interests of a ruling elite seeking to entrench political dominance, with little regard for national unity and cohesion. The same logic applies to those in the current hybrid government pushing to create new provinces and fragment existing ones. This is about control, not reform. True ethnic minorities in some provinces, such as Seraiki speakers in southern Punjab, have long wanted their own province. Some political parties have actively supported this. But the challenge is how to square this with carving out a new unit that could undermine the delicate constitutional balance, spark controversy and encourage others to demand new provinces. The 18th Constitutional Amendment , backed by all parties in 2010, opened a new chapter in provincial empowerment. Over a dozen ministries were devolved from the federal level to the provinces. But this also raised capacity issues and whether provinces could handle the increased fiscal power and resources devolved to them. The fiscal aspect evoked the most criticism. Because with the 2009 National Finance Commission award, the substantial transfer of resources to the provinces left the federal government unable to meet its financial obligations. While this tussle over revenue needs to be resolved and provinces should mobilise their own resources, creating smaller provinces or rolling back the amendment is not the answer. In fact, the rationale for redrawing provincial boundaries remains opaque. This lack of clarity reinforces the impression that the motive is to increase control, not to improve governance. If we want real reform, it’s not by carving out new provinces. It’s by empowering local government. The writer is a former ambassador to the US, UK and UN. Published in Dawn, August 24th, 2026

items.title: Un groupe électrogène en provenance du Sénégal pour aider au rétablissement de l’électricité à Nouakchott
items.description: Un groupe électrogène est arrivé dimanche soir à Rosso, en vue de son transfert vers Nouakchott afin de contribuer au rétablissement de l'approvisionnement en électricité après deux incendies qui ont ravagé deux postes de transformation de la capitale en l'espace de deux jours, selon une source de « Sahara Media ». Le correspondant de « Sahara Media » à Rosso a indiqué que le groupe électrogène était arrivé dimanche soir en provenance du Sénégal et qu’il avait quitté la ville en direction de Nouakchott au sein d’un convoi composé de techniciens et escorté par une unité de la gendarmerie. Le groupe électrogène doit être acheminé vers l’une des deux sous-stations endommagées par l’incendie, dans le cadre des efforts en cours visant à renforcer le réseau électrique et à accélérer le rétablissement du service dans les quartiers qui subissent encore des coupures. Un incendie s’était déclaré dans la sous-station de l’Est, au nord de Nouakchott, avant qu’une autre sous-station de 33/15 kV, située à l’ouest de Nouakchott, ne soit touchée par un autre incendie, provoquant d’importantes coupures d’électricité dans la capitale. La Société mauritanienne d’électricité (Somelec) a indiqué dans son dernier communiqué que ses équipes techniques avaient remis en service la ligne Nouakchott-Idini, qui alimente les puits d’eau potable, et rétabli l’électricité dans d’autres zones grâce à des lignes d’alimentation parallèles et de remplacement. La société a ajouté que de vastes zones de l’ouest de Nouakchott ont commencé à retrouver progressivement l’électricité dimanche soir, en fonction des capacités de charge disponibles sur le réseau, tandis que ses équipes poursuivent la réparation des parties endommagées des cellules de distribution et des disjoncteurs, ainsi que le rétablissement du service dans les autres zones.

items.title: Outgoing Saudi envoy meets president
items.description: Saudi Ambassador Nawaf bin Said Al-Malki calls on President Asif Ali Zardari at Aiwan-i-Sadr.—APP ISLAMABAD: President Asif Ali Zardari on Sunday appreciated the contribution of Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Pakistan Nawaf bin Said Al-Malki towards strengthening the longstanding fraternal and strategic bilateral ties. Ambassador Malki, who has served in Pakistan since 2017, called on the president for a farewell call at Aiwan-i-Sadr. President Zardari expressed appreciation for his dedicated service and the friendship, warmth and cooperation he extended to Pakistan during his tenure. He said the ambassador had played an important role in advancing bilateral relations, particularly in the political, economic and trade spheres. Pakistan deeply values its time-tested friendship and strategic partnership with Saudi Arabia and appreciated the Kingdom’s steadfast support for Pakistan, he said. He also expressed confidence that the strong foundation laid during Ambassador Malki’s tenure would continue to guide bilateral cooperation in the years ahead. Published in Dawn, August 24th, 2026

items.title: Le président mauritanien ordonne au gouvernement de déterminer les causes des pannes électriques dans la capitale et d’en déterminer les responsabilités
items.description: Le président mauritanien Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani a ordonné de déterminer les causes des pannes qui ont touché deux postes de transformation électrique à Nouakchott et d’établir les responsabilités, tout en accordant la priorité au rétablissement du service électrique dans les plus brefs délais, après les coupures généralisées subies par la capitale au cours des deux derniers jours. Dans une déclaration faite à l’issue de sa visite sur l’une des deux sous-stations endommagées, Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani a indiqué avoir donné des instructions « afin de déterminer les causes de ces incidents, d’établir les responsabilités et de prendre toutes les mesures nécessaires pour éviter que de telles pannes ne se reproduisent à l’avenir ». Le président a ajouté qu’il avait chargé le gouvernement de mobiliser tous les moyens humains, techniques et matériels nécessaires et d’accélérer le rythme des interventions, tout en respectant strictement les normes de sécurité et de sûreté. Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani a précisé que la sous-station de l’Est avait repris son fonctionnement, tandis qu’une « solution d’urgence » était mise en œuvre dans la sous-station du Nord afin de la remettre en service dans les plus brefs délais. Les déclarations du président font suite à deux incendies qui ont ravagé vendredi et samedi deux postes de transformation à Nouakchott, provoquant de graves perturbations dans l’approvisionnement en électricité de la capitale et des coupures de courant dans plusieurs quartiers et zones. La Société mauritanienne d’électricité (Somelec) avait annoncé le rétablissement progressif de l’électricité dans plusieurs zones grâce à des lignes d’alimentation de secours, ainsi que la remise en service de la ligne Nouakchott-Idini qui alimente les puits d’eau potable. Le président a insisté sur la nécessité de poursuivre et d’accélérer les efforts visant à moderniser le réseau de distribution d’électricité à Nouakchott, alors que les équipes techniques poursuivent les travaux de réparation des parties endommagées et rétablissent le service dans les zones encore touchées par les coupures.

items.title: Jamaat threatens march on Islamabad over petroleum levy
items.description: • Hafiz Naeem says sit-ins to be converted into shutter-down strike on 13th Rabiul Awwal • Party to stage indefinite protest outside Governor House in Quetta from 29th LAHORE / KARACHI: Jamaat-i-Islami chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Sunday warned the government that the party would expand its ongoing sit-ins into a nationwide movement, culminating in a shutter-down strike and a possible march on Islamabad if the petroleum levy was not withdrawn. Addressing a press conference at the JI sit-in site in Lahore, Mr Rehman said the protests in the provincial capital had entered their eighth day and would continue until the government abolished the petroleum levy. He announced that JI would establish protest camps across the country and call a nationwide shutter-down strike on 13th Rabiul Awwal, followed by a march towards Islamabad if the government failed to respond to its demands. “The rulers are squeezing the blood out of the people through forced levies and taxes,” he said, adding that the government was protecting the privileges of the ruling elite while shifting the burden of its policies onto ordinary citizens. Mr Rehman said public pressure had forced the government to reduce the price of diesel by Rs32 per litre. He said oil mafias had been making excessive profits by charging consumers for imported diesel at rates linked to the cost of locally produced diesel. The JI chief also said the government and sugar mafia were manipulating the sugar market. He said 765,000 tonnes of sugar had been imported in collusion with vested interests without taxes, yet sugar prices continued to rise. He announced that JI would celebrate Eid Miladun Nabi on 12th Rabiul Awwal at the sit-in sites. Series of sit-ins According to a statement issued by the JI from Islamabad, the party announced a series of protest sit-ins across the federal capital as part of its nationwide protest campaign against the petroleum levy, rising fuel prices, inflation and costly agreements with independent power producers. A protest sit-in was staged in the federal capital’s Ghori Town on Sunday. Another sit-in will be staged in Islamabad’s Karachi Company today (Monday), followed by protests in Sector G-7/3 on 25th, B-17 on 27th and the PWD neighbourhood on 28th. The next demonstrations will be held on Aug 29, 30 and 31 in Bharakahu, Jhangi Syedan and Lehtrar Road, respectively. ‘PPP conniving with PML-N’ In Karachi, the JI’s sit-in near Governor House continued for the eighth consecutive day on Sunday, with party leaders insisting that the protest would not be called off unless the government withdrew the petroleum levy and provided relief to consumers. Addressing the protesters, JI Karachi chief Monem Zafar Khan said the party would continue its struggle until the petroleum levy was withdrawn. He maintained that the levy had placed an additional burden on ordinary citizens already struggling with inflation and high utility bills. He also criticised the Sindh government, accusing it of “conniving” with the PML-N-led federal government instead of protecting the interests of people. Meanwhile, the JI Balochistan announced plans to stage an indefinite sit-in outside Governor House in Quetta starting from Aug 29. The protest aims to challenge unfulfilled government promises, high petroleum levy, and rising lawlessness. Speaking at a press conference at the Quetta Press Club, JI Provincial Vice President Zahid Akhtar Baloch said the sit-in would continue until the party’s demands were met. With additional input from Bakhtawar Mian in Islamabad and Muhammad Akbar Notezai in Quetta Published in Dawn, August 24th, 2026
